clue.text: Will's given top place to runner covering the centre of NZ

indicators.note: the runner covers over the middle of the spelt-out country, sitting in place of its central letter

parts.note: the abbreviation spelt out as it is said, also a slang name for New Zealand
a ski is a runner on snow

explanation.surface: A runner given a podium finish in a race through the heart of New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: ENSKIED is a Shakespearean coinage, hence 'Will's'; SKI takes the place of the Z at the centre of ENZED.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensky is to raise to the heavens, so something enskied has been exalted to the highest position, a word found in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Rising temperature among top-flight crew

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top
something among others sits in their midst, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: de luxe means of the highest quality
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: The heat goes up among an elite team of aircrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' looks like a team of people, but it is the past tense of crow, as in boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Crew is a past tense of crow, and to crow is to boast or rejoice triumphantly, the same as exulted.

clue.text: Ball game park takes a new wicket

indicators.note: something new has been made over, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket match in which the park team claims a fresh wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: The wicket's W joins the fodder before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepak takraw is a Southeast Asian sport like volleyball in which players kick a rattan ball over a net.

clue.text: Trendy wine behind bars

parts.note: what is trendy is in fashion
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A fashionable wine served in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind bars' suggests a pub counter; here it means locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: In hock is slang for being in prison, as well as in pawn or in debt.

clue.text: Make intelligible sign in proof that contains substantive bracketing stuff

indicators.note: whatever contains something holds it inside, so the proof sign wraps the rest

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark meaning delete

indicators.note: brackets enclose what lies between them, so the abbreviation goes around the stuff

parts.note: sb is the dictionary abbreviation for substantive, an old name for a noun
to cram is to stuff

explanation.surface: Instructions for a proofreader marking up a document full of brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: Substantive is an old grammar word for a noun, hence the dictionary label sb. The containers nest: the stuffing inside the noun label, all inside the proof mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To descramble a coded or garbled signal is to restore it to a form that can be understood.

clue.text: Scot's whistling in broadcast item from Bow?

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, that is to sow it
a Cockney says fing for thing; Bow is the East London district whose bells define a true Cockney

explanation.surface: A radio piece about East London featuring a whistler.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'item from Bow' is a thing as a Cockney would pronounce it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sowf is a Scottish verb meaning to whistle or hum softly, and sowfing is its present participle.

clue.text: Risky investment urge after double back-shift?

indicators.note: each letter is moved back two places in the alphabet, a double backward shift

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker on the late shift twice over feels tempted to gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: U back two is S, R is P, G is E and E is C. A back shift is also British for an afternoon work shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Spec is short for speculation, a purchase made in the hope of profit but with real risk of loss.

clue.text: Traditional outfitters putting one per cent into wide chapeaux

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside
into marks where the inserted letters end up, inside the hats

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
chapeaux is French for hats
the Roman numeral for one
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned tailors add a small markup to the price of broad-brimmed hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipcat is an old slang name for a tailor, so whipcats are tailors of the old sort.

clue.text: Whiskey drunk by two in New Zealand community

indicators.note: a drink taken in ends up inside the drinker

parts.note: the Roman numeral for two
W is Whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A pair of drinkers share a whisky somewhere in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiskey is the radio code word, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An iwi is a Maori tribe, the largest social grouping of the Maori people of New Zealand.

clue.text: String player succeeded in opening device

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it

parts.note: a gambit is an opening move in chess, a ploy to begin
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A musician makes a success of a clever trick to start the concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambist is a player of the viola da gamba, a bowed stringed instrument held between the knees.

clue.text: Judge of diamond finished holding its middle

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside

parts.note: time is up when it is finished

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter only

parts.note: its points back to diamond, whose central letter of seven is kept

explanation.surface: The baseball official's game is over, still holding the centre of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' points back to diamond, which is also part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ump is short for umpire, the official who judges play on a baseball field, which is called the diamond.

clue.text: He has raced around tiny state for large citrus fruit

indicators.note: going around something encloses it
the element has something new, taking it on in exchange
one thing for another means instead of it, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium
to race is to speed
RI is Rhode Island, the smallest US state
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A man speeds through a little country in search of an enormous orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the element, spelt out in full, and SPERID takes the place of its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A hesperidium is the botanical term for a berry with a leathery rind and segmented pulp, the type of fruit an orange or lemon is.

clue.text: Worry about tribe and king's ebbing mind

indicators.note: the tide ebbs by going back out, so the whole is read backwards
about means surrounding, so the worry goes around the rest

parts.note: what is eating you is worrying you
a race is a people or tribe
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Anxiety about his people is wearing down a king's sanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind' reads as a noun but is the imperative verb: be careful.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind as a warning means be careful, and take care is the everyday phrase for the same caution.

clue.text: Round instruments displaying colourful spots

parts.note: O is round in shape
celli is the Italian plural of cello

explanation.surface: A circle of musicians showing off brightly patterned costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocelli are eye-like markings of colour on a butterfly's wing or a peacock's tail, as well as simple eyes in insects.

clue.text: Liberal overturned European claim with one working in bacteria

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal

indicators.note: the reversed claim comes with another piece set in it
placed in something means set inside it
turned over in a down entry, so the letters run upwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
to allege is to claim
the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A Liberal reverses a European claim, with an official working on bacteria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European claim' is reversed as one unit, and the one working sits just after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Legionellae are rod-shaped bacteria of the genus Legionella, which causes Legionnaires' disease.

clue.text: Who might revise cities in Korea's borders?

definitions.text: Who might revise cities in Korea's borders?

indicators.note: to revise is to rework, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a country's borders are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Korea

explanation.surface: A question about who might replan cities along Korea's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: such a planner might well redesign cities.
explanation.definitionFit: An ekistician studies ekistics, the science of human settlements, and so could be called on to replan towns and cities.

clue.text: Ocker's ugly character is reflected

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front

parts.note: a card is a character, an eccentric person

explanation.surface: An Australian's unattractive personality shows in his face.
explanation.walkthrough: Ocker is a stereotypical uncultivated Australian, so this is an Australian slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Drac is Australian slang for unattractive, said to come from Dracula's looks.

clue.text: Fire door should be high on joint, maybe

parts.note: a cannabis joint is something to smoke; maybe signals an example
tight is slang for drunk, close to high

explanation.surface: Someone guarding a fire door gets stoned on a spliff.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so 'high' follows the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire door must be smoketight, sealed so that no fumes can pass through it during a blaze.

clue.text: Rip off George Cross collection for ten a penny

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
GC is the abbreviation for the George Cross, a British gallantry award
a heap is a pile or collection

explanation.surface: Cheating a medal collector by selling decorations at bargain prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten a penny is a British idiom for something so plentiful that it is almost worthless, very cheap indeed.

clue.text: "Work pounds" included in what's said to be cutting fibre in muscle

definitions.note: loose: it is the cytoplasm inside a muscle fibre

indicators.note: something included in another is held inside it

parts.note: sarcasm is commonly called cutting
op is short for opus, a work
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A trainer's sharp remark about effort pounding the muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'Work pounds' are two separate abbreviations kept together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcoplasm is the specialised cytoplasm that fills each muscle cell, the material within the fibre.

clue.text: MS treatment posed the author distress

parts.note: a model who posed sat for the artist
the writer refers to themself as I
to vex is to trouble or distress

explanation.surface: A writer upset that a medical treatment was even suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: Sativex is a cannabis-based mouth spray prescribed to relieve muscle stiffness in multiple sclerosis.

clue.text: Cape's head covering like hood with front halves trimmed back

indicators.note: back means the result is read in the other direction
cutting off the front half of each word leaves only its second half

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cape worn on the head, like a hood with its front cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: LIKE becomes KE and HOOD becomes OD. The Cape is South Africa's Cape Province, where Afrikaans is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A doek is a South African headscarf, from the Afrikaans word for cloth.

clue.text: Rusk has violated dietary rules

indicators.note: something violated is broken, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eating a rusk breaks someone's food laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashrus is the Ashkenazi form of kashrut, the body of Jewish law governing which foods are kosher.

clue.text: Thrilled to accept Curie as knowledgeable earlier

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in

parts.note: sent is slang for thrilled or carried away
Ci is the symbol for the curie, a unit of radioactivity

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to welcome Marie Curie as a learned guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Curie is the unit, not the scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Scient is an obsolete adjective meaning learned or skilled, hence the earlier in the definition.

clue.text: Hard-hitting report from Scouse pal on Thursday

parts.note: Th is the abbreviation for Thursday
wack is Liverpool slang for a mate; Scouse is the Liverpool dialect

explanation.surface: A Liverpudlian friend files a hard-hitting story on Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' suggests a news piece, but it is the noise of a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A thwack is the sharp sound of a heavy blow, a report made by hard hitting.

clue.text: To preserve affluent London area, each leaves deer-hunting circles

parts.note: to tin food is to preserve it

indicators.note: what leaves departs, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: Chelsea is a wealthy district of London
ea is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Rich Londoners leave their smart set to go deer hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinchel is a Scottish ring of hunters who encircle deer and gradually close in on them.

clue.text: Burns brought up Selkirk Grace in "Caledonian" to start with

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means read from the bottom upward
the start of each word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: At a Burns Supper someone recites the Selkirk Grace, a short prayer before the Scottish meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' looks like the poet but is the definition: burns are cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Burn is British slang for tobacco or a cigarette, so burns are smokes.

clue.text: Buyer holds note bearing name of first month

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside

parts.note: the vendee is the buyer in a sale
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up a banknote carrying the name of January.
explanation.definitionFit: Vendemiaire, the vintage month, was the first month of the French Republican calendar, beginning in late September.

clue.text: Ancestor protected by guardian angel?

indicators.note: something protected by words is held within them, out of sight

parts.note: the end of guardian and start of angel

explanation.surface: A forebear watched over by a heavenly protector.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that a grandmother can be a family's guardian angel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is an informal name for a grandmother, a direct forebear two generations back.

clue.text: We must leave inferior crumbs

indicators.note: what must leave is taken away

parts.note: lower in rank is inferior
taken as written

explanation.surface: We have to leave poor-quality breadcrumbs behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs' is not bread but an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lor is a dated British exclamation of surprise, a shortening of Lord, just as crumbs is.

clue.text: Relations keeping on about frogs once used for pregnancy testing

definitions.text: frogs once used for pregnancy testing

indicators.note: turned about means faced the other way, so read backwards
keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: sexual relations
upon means on

explanation.surface: Family members carrying on about frogs from old-fashioned pregnancy tests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests family, but is a euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenopus is the genus of African clawed frogs, which ovulate when injected with a pregnant woman's urine, the basis of an early test.

clue.text: Small stone cask around evergreen trees

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a gem is a precious stone
a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: A little rock and a barrel lie among the evergreens.
explanation.definitionFit: The nutmeg is a tropical evergreen tree whose seed gives the spice, so nutmegs are such trees.
